The French Thales Defense and Security was chosen for the acquisition of new 3D early warning radars. 5 GM400α stationary & 2 GM400α mobile systems will be used by the Bulgarian Air Force. The deal was approved by the Bulgarian parliament on November 26, 2025. The competition for the radars has been withdrawn. The deal for seven radars, capped at 195 million Euro, will be signed by the Bulgarian and French government, the Bulgarian partner on the French side will not be the manufacturer, but the Direction générale de l'armement and will be partially financed through the Security Action for Europe financial instrument. The first three radars will be delivered in August, September and December 2027 and the other four will follow until the end of 2029. These new radars will replace the obsolete P-18 and P-37 currently in service.
1 SLM system ordered & 5 SLM systems approved

New surface-to-air missile systems to replace older S-200 & S-300 systems. In 2024, the Bulgarian government signed an order for one medium range IRIS-T SLM system comprising three fire units, radar and command vehicles for 179 million Euro to be delivered by the end of 2027. Along with the order came the option of additional five SLM systems and one long range SLX system. On October 14, 2026, the Bulgarian government approved the purchase of the optional five SLM systems by amending the total contract value including the first SLM system to 1.139 billion Euro to be financed through the Security Action for Europe program. The government has identified in its armed forces modernization program a requirement for an additional two medium range systems and two more long range systems.
